prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1449; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound on a two-lane county road in Pearland, Texas, when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 crossed into the northbound lane and made frontal contact with Driver 1's vehicle. Both vehicles were moving at low speed at the time of impact. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was transported for evaluation. The nature of the impact and the forces involved appear consistent with the reported injury. Damage to both vehicles is largely consistent with a frontal collision of this type. Responding officers photographed the scene and the vehicles, and the photographs confirm several details of the crash. No independent witnesses were identified. Driver 1 was the operator of the vehicle, and records show Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the applicable policy. A Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle, but it could not be fully determined from statements or the scene where the Passenger and Driver 1 were seated at the moment of impact. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to the reporting officer.
